post.caption: Tiffany bought many of France's crown jewels. In May 1887 France's young republic held the sale at the Louvre, because it wanted to prevent a royalist return. The lots included Empress Eugénie's currant-leaf diamond set, and Charles Lewis Tiffany of New York bought a large share. Estimates of his share run from one third to over two thirds. Tiffany shipped the jewels to New York in special leather boxes embossed with the French for Diamonds of the Crown, and wealthy American families such as the Pulitzers later bought pieces. Afterward the press reportedly called him the King of Diamonds.
